stem.en: Look at the free-body diagram of the 4 kg block sitting on the frictionless table, from this lesson's table-and-pulley setup. Which of these is the ONLY horizontal force acting on it?

feedback.en: Weight always points straight down — it has no horizontal part here.

text.en: The normal force from the table

feedback.en: The normal force is the table pushing straight up — that's vertical, not horizontal.
Right — the string pulls the block horizontally toward the pulley. It's the only force in that direction, so it alone determines the block's horizontal acceleration.

explanation.en: Weight and the normal force are both vertical and cancel each other. Tension is the only force pulling sideways, so T = m₁a for the table block.

hints.en: Draw the table block's free-body diagram first: which forces point up/down, and which point sideways?
Only a force that pulls it toward or away from the pulley counts as horizontal here.
